newsitem.title: MEXICO: Seized drugs stolen by Mexican officials.
newsitem.headline: Seized drugs stolen by Mexican officials.

text.p: Mexican officials helped steal nearly half a tonne of cocaine in the northern state of Sonora that was seized from drug traffickers, Mexico's Attorney General's Office (PGR) said on Thursday.

In a fresh blow to Mexico's scandal-hit anti-drug efforts, the PGR said it arrested at least seven officials involved in the May 21 heist in the border town of San Luis Rio Colorado, a few miles (kilometers) south of Yuma, Arizona.

The seven men were federal government prosecutors, federal police and, in one case, a military official, the PGR said in a statement. It said several other officials had been placed under house arrest while the investigation continued.
The drugs had not yet been recovered.
"According to our investigations, the men wilfully created the conditions for the drugs to be taken out of the local offices of the PGR in San Luis Rio Colorado, Sonora," the statement said.
Police assumed initially that narcotraffickers had broken into the local offices of the PGR to steal some 1,045 pounds (476 kg) of cocaine that had been seized just days before.
But police found the local officials living a lavish lifestyle following the incident.

"From the men, police have recovered $132,870 in cash, several Rolex watches worth $12,000, a bank account with 80,000 pesos ($10,000) and $4,000, as well as a truck and a car -- all the product of their illicit activities," it said.

Mexico is a main conduit for illegal drugs from South America to the United States and has recently suffered a string of drug corruption scandals. Mexico's main anti-drugs official was arrested on corruption charges in February.
